chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: Duke suggests the Fender bass; Jackson's memorized book
summary: Ellington urged him to take up Fender bass when he couldn't play trombone; Jackson says he memorized every arrangement.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yes. And I had a ball that day and that's when Duke asked me why didn't I go play the fender bass, because he knew I played bass. He said, 'Why don't you get a fender bass? You can't play the trombone now.' He said, 'Why don't you get a fender bass and come with me?' I said, 'I don't have one.'
What a beautiful man, you know, at

Oh, beautiful. And I used to just -- you played that music and you became so engrossed in that music, you became very engrossed in that music. That's the reason I memorized like I did. I never had to open my book. I never did. Once the valet left my book in a town and Duke said, "Can you play [ ]?" I said, "Go ahead and play." I remembered every arrangement in there.
